fields.description: Which bench to install into. Only benches found by the last scan appear here.
fields.label: Bench

fields.description: Org + Repo builds an SSH URL through the configured host alias for that organisation, which is what pins the right key. Use Git URL only for a remote that is not one of yours.
fields.label: Source

fields.description: Determines which SSH key is offered. Getting this wrong produces 'Repository not found' on a repository you can definitely see in a browser.
fields.label: Organisation

fields.description: Just the repository name, e.g. gh_erp — not the full URL.
fields.label: Repository

fields.description: A full git remote, e.g. git@github.com:org/repo.git or https://github.com/org/repo.git
fields.label: Git URL

fields.description: Leave blank for the repository's default branch.
fields.label: Branch

fields.description: Derived from the repository name and passed to bench explicitly, so it never has to guess the app name out of an SSH host alias.
fields.label: App Name

fields.description: The exact remote that will be cloned, after the organisation alias is applied.
fields.label: Resolved URL

fields.description: Leave this on. Building assets is by far the largest memory consumer in a bench operation, and on a small server it is the step most likely to take the machine down. Run `bench build --app <name>` by hand when the box is idle.
fields.label: Skip Asset Build

fields.description: If the app directory already exists, replace it. bench ARCHIVES the old copy to archived/apps/<name>-<date> rather than deleting it, so nothing is lost.
fields.label: Overwrite If Present

fields.description: Optional. After a successful clone, run bench --site <site> install-app. Leave blank to only place the code on disk.
fields.label: Install On Site

fields.description: Passes --force to install-app. Only needed when reinstalling an app the site already has.
fields.label: Force Install
Status
fields.options:
Draft
Queued
Running
Success
Failed
Cancelled

fields.description: The authoritative success signal — 0 succeeded, above 0 the command failed, -1 means it never ran because a pre-flight refused it. stdout and stderr are interleaved in the log for readability, so the log text can never be used to decide whether it worked.
fields.label: Exit Code

fields.description: The exact argv that was executed, so it can be reproduced by hand in a terminal.
fields.label: Command
